Both windows could work from our side, but to give your team the most value I recommend a 90-minute slot for the first working session (intros, success criteria, prompt review, routing strategy) plus a separate 60–90 minute lab for hands-on prompt tuning and a later load test window. - Option B: Thu, Sep 18 — 10:00–11:30 PT (90m) — in case you need a slightly later slot

Agenda (draft):
1) 10m — stakeholder intros & roles

3) 30m — prompt collection & review (bring representative prompts)
4) 20m — routing/topology discussion (models, failover, latency SLOs)

For the load test we typically ask for:
- target RPS and expected peak concurrency
- representative prompt length distribution
- whether Quanta wants on-hosted or Redwood-managed load generation

I’ll draft a mutual action plan and a load-test runbook and attach before the meeting.

Best,

Subject: Re: Pilot onramp — proposed kickoff windows — load test notes

Quick technical notes from my side so we can size the pilot correctly:

- For an initial smoke load test we typically aim for 5–10 RPS sustained for 10 minutes, then a ramp to target peak for 3–5 minutes. For an actual production-like test you should expect 50–200 RPS depending on model choice.
- Please share: expected average prompt token length, percentile (p95) latency SLO, and whether you need token-level cost projections.
- If Quanta wants Redwood to run the load from our side, we need network egress IPs and an allowlist; if you’ll run it from your infra, we’ll provide the load harness and metrics endpoints.
- Model variants: please indicate if you need quantized variants or only FP16/FP32 — that affects instance selection.

If you confirm the preferred kickoff slot, I’ll add a short appendix to the runbook with exact curl examples and a small sample dataset.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Lead Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
